title: Character lab: 8 simple female character designs, ranked for pixel feasibility
question: Owner: start over from character design with simpler characters. Which designs are most feasible as pixel-art sprites across body presets (chibi, compact, slim) and complexity tiers?
method: 8 specs (astronaut, short-haired girl, schoolgirl, diver, mechanic, plus courier, ranger and runner) written in a shared primitive vocabulary (charlab/designs/VOCAB.md): body preset + build, hair style from a vocabulary of 6, eyes+brows-only face, 10-12 colour palette, pieces as cover shells or primitives with colour roles, simple/medium/detailed tier lists, and 0-2 secondary parts. One Gemini concept call per character (8 calls, front + 3/4 view). Small-size check: area-downscale of the concepts to 32/48/64 px.
result: 8 JSON specs, with 3-6 pieces in the simple tier, 8-12 in detailed, and at most 2 secondary parts each (3 characters have none). The concepts came out clean and on-palette. At small size, the diver is a thin dark figure that loses its read, and the ranger's olive/khaki blurs.
verdict: Ranking: 1 Mika (short hair), 2 Kai (runner), 3 Hana (schoolgirl), 4 Rio (mechanic), 5 Nova (astronaut), 6 Fern (ranger), 7 Zip (courier), 8 Marin (diver). Suggest building Mika at the simple tier first, then Kai (slim) and Nova (chibi) to compare presets.
